title: Forest model estimates measured stool microbial abundance
summary: A random forest estimated measured abundance from sample-level data. In a separate 179-sample cohort, predicted and measured values had R² 0.92. The result validates a specific measurement relationship rather than a disease diagnosis.
organization: Stanford University; University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

evidence.tested: Development used 518 samples; a separate Parkinson’s-disease/control cohort supplied179 samples. Nested cross-validation tuned the model.
evidence.unknown: The target is 16S copies per extraction, not cell counts per gram. Processing differences, dynamic-range limits and repeated-sample grouping constrain generalization; operational assay procedures and supplements were not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: The forest learns the association between DNA concentration, broad composition features and reference abundance.

source_review.scope: Computational model Methods, nonactionable measurement Results and limitations; primary front/date/status.
